name: dose-response-crossparadigm
claim: Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.
experiment: Sweep the initial viral load via `infected_seed.fraction` in {0.03, 0.08, 0.15} (seeding 1, 3, 5 infected cells of the 36-cell block) on the Sego blueprint, over rules-seeds {0, 1}, on BOTH backends at reduced scale (N=120). Record the final infected-cell count and check that the highest dose ends with strictly more infection than the lowest, on each backend and seed.
result: Seeding 1 / 3 / 5 infected cells, final infected counts (N=120): CPM seed0 1/2/7, CPM seed1 1/3/2, vertex seed0 0/2/5, vertex seed1 1/3/6. The lowest-vs-highest direction is STRICT in all four (backend, seed) cases (final_high > final_low), so both backends agree on the direction. Intermediate monotonicity is NOT universal (CPM seed1 is 1/3/2), so only the directional (low-vs-high) claim is made. CPM and vertex magnitudes are comparable and within the capstone's same-seed spread.

purpose.question: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?
purpose.mechanism: More initially-infected cells secrete more virus into the shared field, raising the per-cell infection probability (Pr = 1 - exp(-g_hv * virus)) everywhere, so the final infected count rises with the initial dose on either substrate.
purpose.expected_outcome: A strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose on both backends and seeds (directional agreement), with magnitudes comparable across substrates.

key_assumptions: Initial viral load is proxied by the number of initially-infected cells (infected_seed.fraction); the ODE v0 input has no field producer at this scale.
Rates are the faithful Sego values (no tuning); the epidemic is slow, so the demonstration runs 120 steps over seeds {0,1}.
Directional (lowest-vs-highest, strict) agreement is the target; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and NOT claimed.

limitations: Directional (lowest-vs-highest) only: intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent (CPM seed1 is 1/3/2), so a dose-response CURVE is not claimed.
Initial load is proxied by seeded infected cells; the ODE v0 virus input has no producer, so a true viral-titre dose axis is deferred (Task 21).
Three doses, two seeds, reduced scale/steps -- enough to establish the direction, not a dose-response fit; magnitudes are within the capstone's same-seed spread.

report.title: Dose-response: both substrates agree on the strict direction
report.verdict: Over initial viral loads seeding 1/3/5 infected cells, the highest dose ends with STRICTLY more infection than the lowest on both backends and both seeds (CPM 1/2/7 & 1/3/2, vertex 0/2/5 & 1/3/6 at N=120), so the two substrates agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response. Intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent (CPM seed1), so only the directional (low-vs-high) claim is made. Magnitudes are comparable and within the capstone's same-seed spread.
report.main_insight: The shared field makes the dose-response DIRECTION backend-independent (more seed virus -> higher infection probability everywhere); the substrate affects only the (noisy) magnitude.
report.caveat: Three doses, two seeds, reduced scale; the dose axis is seeded-cell count, not a viral titre (ODE v0 has no producer yet); only the strict low-vs-high direction is claimed.

findings.statement: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 0->5 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.
findings.explanation: More seed virus raises the shared-field infection probability everywhere; the substrate sets only the noisy magnitude.
findings.next_action: revisit magnitudes once the ODE V producer lands (Task 21)
